source_ref: Eskenazi, Askew & Folk (2023), Behav Res Methods 55(2):623-632, doi:10.3758/s13428-022-01834-3 (Method, Study 1, read from the Springer article page); OSF osf.io/7tuwr (view_only link in the IRW dictionary): Study1.xlsx (header row 1 = the 109 target words), Supplemental Materials.xlsx (per-item 'Accuracy (M)'), Lexical Expertise Code.R; IRW processing script data/spelling assessment_study1.R
note: Spelling dictation task. The IRW item code IS the Study1.xlsx column header (data/spelling assessment_study1.R pivots every non-ID column straight into item), and each header is the target word itself, so item_text reproduces the code verbatim and no code->text inference exists. item_text is the word that was SPOKEN to participants, not text they read: per the paper, 'Recordings were created for each of the 110 words such that each word was spoken clearly three times. Two words were determined to have multiple possible pronunciations, and thus were spoken four times' (the paper does not say which two). instructions is the paper's own third-person description of the instruction ('Participants were instructed to listen to each word spoken three (or four) times and to spell that word by typing it into the space provided.'), not the on-screen wording, which is not in the deposit. resp is binary accuracy; option_text Incorrect=0 / Correct=1 and correct_response=1 follow the paper's correct/incorrect scoring (megart_tonkovic_2021 / twod_rotation_mather2023 precedent). Direction confirmed: live per-item percent resp=1 matches the supplement's Study 1 'Accuracy (M)' to within 0.19 points for 106 of 108 shared items (median |diff| 0.13), e.g. hydraulic 42.29, moustache 94.98. The 110th word, occident, was excluded by the authors (heterographic homophone of oxidant) and is absent from both Study1.xlsx and the live table. DISCREPANCY (not a mapping defect in IRW): the supplement's Study 1 accuracy column gives annihilate 86.73 / anatomic 45.80, while the data file's own columns give annihilate 45.39 (305/672) / anatomic 86.78 (584/673) -- the two values are exchanged. The data-file labels are taken as correct: Study1.xlsx is alphabetical except for exactly this pair (col 12 annihilate, col 13 anatomic), which is what a column-order colMeans pasted against an alphabetical label list would swap; Study2.xlsx (independent sample, n=785) gives annihilate 54.65, consistent with the data-file label and not with 86.7; and annihilate (double n) is the harder spelling. IRW ships the data file's labels unchanged.
public_note: Words were presented aurally (each spoken three or four times) and typed by participants; item_text is the target word, and instructions paraphrase the procedure as the paper reports it rather than the on-screen wording.
